'''''Significant Figures: The Lives and Work of Great Mathematicians''''' is a 2017 nonfiction book by British mathematician  [[Ian Stewart (mathematician)|Ian Stewart]] {{post-nominals|country=GBR|FRS|CMath|FIMA}}, published by [[Basic Books]].<ref>{{Cite book| publisher = Basic Books| isbn = 978-0-465-09612-1 |oclc=1030547312| last1 = Stewart| first1 = Ian| last2 = Basic Books| title = Significant Figures: the lives and work of great mathematicians| location = New York| date = 2017 |pages=303}}</ref> In the work, Stewart discusses the lives and contributions of 25 figures who are prominent in the history of mathematics.<ref>{{cite web|author=Hunacek, Mark|title=Review of ''Significant Figures'' by Ian Stewart|website=MAA Reviews, Mathematical Association of America|date=22 September 2017|url=https://www.maa.org/press/maa-reviews/significant-figures}}</ref> The 25 mathematicians selected are: [[Archimedes]], [[Liu Hui]], [[Muḥammad ibn Mūsā al-Khwārizmī]], [[Madhava of Sangamagrama]], [[Gerolamo Cardano]], [[Pierre de Fermat]], [[Isaac Newton]], [[Leonhard Euler|Euler]], [[Joseph Fourier|Fourier]], [[Carl Friedrich Gauss|Gauss]], [[Nikolai Lobachevsky|Lobachevsky]], [[Évariste Galois|Galois]], [[Ada Lovelace]], [[George Boole|Boole]], [[Bernhard Riemann|Riemann]], [[Georg Cantor|Cantor]], [[Sofya Kovalevskaya|Sofia Kovalevskaia]], [[Henri Poincaré|Poincaré]], [[David Hilbert|Hilbert]], [[Emmy Noether]], [[Srinivasa Ramanujan|Ramanujan]], [[Kurt Gödel|Gödel]], [[Alan Turing|Turing]], [[Benoit Mandelbrot|Mandelbrot]], and [[William Thurston|Thurston]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Review of ''Significant Figures''|author=Bultheel, Adhemar|date=20 July 2017|website=European Mathematical Society|url=https://euro-math-soc.eu/review/significant-figures}}</ref>

==Reception==
In ''Kirkus Reviews'', it was written that "even a popularizer as skilled and prolific as Stewart cannot expect general readers to fully digest his highly distilled explanations of what these significant figures did to resolve ever more complex conundrums as math advanced." However, the reviewer praised Stewart's sketches of the lives and times of the innovators. The book was described as "a text for teachers, precocious students, and intellectually curious readers unafraid to tread unfamiliar territory".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.kirkusreviews.com/book-reviews/ian-stewart/significant-figures/|title=Significant Figures: The Lives and Work of Great Mathematicians|work=Kirkus Reviews|language=en-us|date=15 July 2017|access-date = 6 January 2024}}</ref>
